treatment.logline: A returned phone opens a small space for mutual interest, until a family demand closes it again.

arc.feeling: Ordinary intimacy gives way to compliance and distance.
Warmth survives, but neither can prolong the encounter.

treatment.approach: Grounded romantic drama: an unhurried roadside exchange is interrupted by a private phone demand. Begin with shared frames, isolate Anudi during the call, and return to shared space for the farewell. Believable rain-sky side light, gentle facial modelling and restrained colour serve D01 and D17; do not impose thriller lighting. Source takes exceed target because dialogue and essential actions remain intact.

treatment.geography: Anudi stays frame left, looking right; Kasun stays frame right, looking left. The food three-wheeler is behind Kasun on the right. Cameras remain on the road-facing side of their axis. Anudi departs toward the left background; Kasun returns toward the right background. Anudi carries the open umbrella in her left hand and the handbag on her left forearm, leaving her right hand free for the phone; Kasun initially offers it in his right hand.

The phone display is essential story information, readable before the private voice.

editor_notes: The bin contains 12 must sources totalling 80 seconds, under the 81-second cap. The 45-second stated scene length is shorter than the supplied 53-second script timing; do not trim or split a line to force it. Source takes include handles and are not the finished running time.

A and G shared frames establish the handover, business and later altered encounter; B and C/E singles and listener shots carry the personal turns. D places the readable incoming caller ID and the preceding impressed reaction together. F closes on the two paths.

The handover transfers the smartphone from Kasun's right hand to Anudi's right hand without hand contact. Anudi keeps the open umbrella in her left hand and her handbag on her left forearm. Match these positions, the same vehicle and the prior-scene cast appearance and wardrobe throughout.

The phone is already beside Anudi's chin at the start of D, already at her ear in the greeting, and already lowered at the start of A after the call. Bridge those off-cut repositionings with eyelines and audio, not a repeated prop action. In D keep screen and face close together at deep focus; the screen text is Father. Start the ring there before the private voice.

Keep L1–L2 and L8–L9 intact within their respective shots. Carry L13 and L14 on the wider listener, then change size for L15; the caller is never pictured. Keep L15 whole, let the smile fade before L17, and give Kasun only her visible expression to react to.

Match the direction of Anudi's look to the food vehicle and the left/right eyelines across G, A and B. The final wide begins after she has oriented toward her route; use Kasun's reverse as the bridge. His pause precedes his return toward the business.
Build rain, road wash, ring and footsteps in sound post, especially under silent-source material; retain clean, private phone-channel audio without placing the caller in the roadside space.

Speed ramps, freeze frames, digital punch-ins and split screens are post-only options, not requested in the source shots; these clean frames permit them if editorial chooses. Avoid applying them merely for decoration.
Avoid mirrors, fast finger work, bodily contact and complex generated screen interaction. The call-ending gesture is one deliberate touch; no extra person, dialogue or action is added.

editor_notes: The bin contains 12 must sources totalling 80 seconds, under the 81-second cap. The 45-second stated scene length is shorter than the supplied 53-second script timing; do not trim or split a line to force it. Source takes include handles and are not the finished running time.

A and G shared frames establish the handover, business and later altered encounter; B and C/E singles and listener shots carry the personal turns. D places the readable incoming caller ID and the preceding impressed reaction together. F closes on the two paths.

The handover transfers the smartphone from Kasun's right hand to Anudi's right hand without hand contact. Anudi keeps the open umbrella in her left hand and her handbag on her left forearm. Match these positions, the same vehicle and the prior-scene cast appearance and wardrobe throughout.

The phone is already beside Anudi's chin at the start of D, already at her ear in the greeting, and already lowered at the start of A after the call. Bridge those off-cut repositionings with eyelines and audio, not a repeated prop action. In D keep screen and face close together at deep focus; the screen text is Father. Start the ring there before the private voice.

Keep L1–L2 and L8–L9 intact within their respective shots. Carry L13 and L14 on the wider listener, then change size for L15; the caller is never pictured. Keep L15 whole, let the smile fade before L17, and give Kasun only her visible expression to react to.

Match the direction of Anudi's look to the food vehicle and the left/right eyelines across G, A and B. The final wide begins after she has oriented toward her route; use Kasun's reverse as the bridge. His pause precedes his return toward the business.
Build rain, road wash, ring and footsteps in sound post, especially under silent-source material; retain clean, private phone-channel audio without placing the caller in the roadside space.

Speed ramps, freeze frames, digital punch-ins and split screens are post-only options, not requested in the source shots; these clean frames permit them if editorial chooses. Avoid applying them merely for decoration.
Avoid mirrors, fast finger work, bodily contact and complex generated screen interaction. The call-ending gesture is one deliberate touch; no extra person, dialogue or action is added.

A gentle rising view lets the two departures and the space between them close the scene.

The existing medium listener provides the first stage of isolation; the closer addition is reserved for the final incoming part.
